sentences.text: The petitioners have prayed for a direction to the respondents to make payment of compensation of the land and building in respect of Arazi nos.1 and 2 situated in Village- Vishunpur-Hasilpur (Indira Nagar, Chhibramau), Tehsil- Chhibramau, District- Kannauj and to release the compensation amount in their favour at the circle rate of the year 2017 treating the land to be commercial.
Other ancillary reliefs have also been claimed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is not disputed that on a previous occasion, the petitioners filed Writ-C No.36333 of 2023 for a direction to the respondents to pay compensation to them.

The said writ petition was filed after passing of an order dated 12.06.2023 by the District Magistrate wherein he observed that it shall be open to the petitioners to approach the Competent Authority, Land Acquisition, Kanpur Nagar with relevant documents to establish their title so that their request for compensation could be considered.
The said writ petition was disposed of as withdrawn with liberty to the petitioners to avail such other remedy as may be advised.
The petitioners instead of availing other remedies again approached this Court by filing Writ-C No.44150 of 2023.
The said writ petition was dismissed by judgement dated 31.05.2024 by a Co-ordinate Bench without prejudice to the rights of the petitioners to approach the Authorities claiming compensation.
It seems that the petitioners in pursuance of the said liberty again approached the Authorities for release of compensation for the acquired land in their favour.

Since, the compensation amount has not been released so far and,
therefore, the instant petition has been filed.
3. The acquisition of the land of the petitioners was under the provisions of the National Highways Act.

Indisputably, an award was passed on 28.02.2022.
4.
From the documents annexed with the writ petition, it is evident that there is serious dispute of title between the petitioners and other persons.

The petitioners have, admittedly, instituted a suit for cancellation of sale deeds executed by their family members in favour of third parties alleging that the aforesaid sales were made in excess of the share of the family members and it wrongly included the share of the petitioners.
Thus, as on date, it is admitted to the petitioners that their other family members had transferred the land in respect of which the petitioners are claiming compensation.
The claim for compensation, therefore, cannot be sustained, at this stage, unless the suit is decreed in favour of the petitioners.
5. It further transpires that there are three other civil suits pending between the parties in respect of the same land.
The remedy of the petitioners was under Section 3H(4) of the National Highways Act to seek reference of the dispute but it seems that they have not availed the said remedy so far.

6. Learned Standing counsel has placed on record the written instructions received from ADM (Land Acqusition) in which also the stand taken is that the compensation amount has not been released because of pending litigation between the parties.

7. In view of serious dispute in respect of title over the subject land, we decline to issue any direction to the respondents for release of compensation in favour of the petitioners as prayed for in the instant petition.
8. The petitioners are free to avail the remedy provided under law.
9. Disposed of accordingly.
(Anish Kumar Gupta, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.)
